title: Words of 2020! (and Metaphors, and Interfaces of the Year)

reader_summary.headline: Hi, everyone, welcome to the A6 and Z podcast.
reader_summary.overview: Hi, everyone, welcome to the A6 and Z podcast. I'm Sonal, and today we have a sort of holiday special episode, a real celebration, or maybe not a celebration, actually. And it's all about the keywords, metaphors and tools of the year, including, of course, the underlying tech shifts.

key_points.text: And our guest is Gretchen McCulloch, who is widely described as an internet linguist.
key_points.evidence_quote: And our guest is Gretchen McCulloch, who is widely described as an internet linguist.

key_points.text: She has a master in linguistics and also wrote the New York Times bestselling book, because internet.
key_points.evidence_quote: She has a master in linguistics and also wrote the New York Times bestselling book, because internet, understanding the new rules of language last year, and because she's so enthusiastic, about linguistics.

key_points.text: She also has a podcast that she co-created called Lingthusiasm.
key_points.evidence_quote: She also has a podcast that she co-created called Lingthusiasm.

key_points.text: We spend roughly the first half of this hallway-style conversation doing a whirlwind tour through the words and metaphors of the year.
key_points.evidence_quote: We spend roughly the first half of this hallway-style conversation doing a whirlwind tour through the words and metaphors of the year, chunked into the themes of remote work, the pandemic, of course, and scientific discourse, key cultural concepts and shifts, and a couple quick personal favorites.

thesis: The episode explores the linguistic shifts and new terminology that emerged in 2020, driven by the pandemic and underlying technology platform changes. It discusses how dictionaries handled the selection of words for the year, noting the unprecedented decision by Oxford to forgo a single word while others like Merriam-Webster and Dictionary.com chose 'pandemic'.
